items.title: 180B Parameters, 32GB of RAM: Pushing MoE Inference to the Limit with Transformers
items.summary_1line: 180B Parameters, 32GB of RAM: Pushing MoE Inference to the Limit with Transformers
items.editor_note: Brings expert streaming into mainstream Transformers at a 180B-to-32GB ratio.

editorial.tldr: This is a pattern across independent work, not one event: early November brought an NVIDIA post on fitting a 124B MoE onto one DGX Spark and a Show HN project, MoEShift, claiming faster MoE inference with half the RAM. A Nov 13 arXiv paper then took the same data-movement problem to TPUs with a fused kernel that also balances uneven expert loads.
editorial.whats_new: Hugging Face (Nov 18) describes expert streaming in Transformers that runs a 180B-parameter MoE in 32GB of RAM, the largest model-to-memory ratio in this thread.
editorial.why_it_matters: MoE serving is bound by moving expert weights, not FLOPs, so memory traffic and expert load balance decide which models fit your hardware and how fast they run.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before sizing hardware for an MoE, measure peak memory and expert-load traffic with streaming on and off; parameter count alone will mislead you.
